    Pulse Rifle¶

    "What the fuck is this pulse rifle doing here." — Emrys, age 6, upon seeing Amelia's weapon for the first time

    The Pulse Rifle is a relic from the Glorious Alliance — a handheld energy weapon carried by the ship's security forces during the Last Great War. In a world of swords, spells, and medieval politics, it is an impossibility. And yet one remains.

    On Ge'or, it is known only to a handful of people — and to Amelia, who calls it a lightning bow.

    Origin — The Ship's Armory¶

    The Glorious Alliance was a Hybrian-built arcology battleship carrying 20 million refugees. Its armory held a limited stock of pulse rifles — standard-issue security weapons, designed for shipboard combat. They fired concentrated energy bolts with no projectile, no casing, no ballistic arc. Clean. Silent. Lethal.

    When the ship was sabotaged by Captain Mad-Dog, when Xiumi overrode the course into the black hole, when the ship emerged 15,000 years before the present and struck Ge'or and its moon — the armory was not a priority. Eight million died in the impact. Four million escaped in pods. Most weapons were abandoned.

    Very few pulse rifles made it into the escape pods. Even fewer survived the fifteen millennia that followed.

    Survival on Ge'or¶

    The pulse rifles that landed on Ge'or faced a world that should have destroyed them:

    • Humidity, sediment, corrosion — fifteen thousand years of burial in caves, swamps, and ruins
    • No maintenance — no one on Ge'or knew how to service them
    • No ammunition — the original power cells degraded within decades

    But the rifles had one saving grace: Ge'or is saturated with magic.

    The black agent dispersed into the atmosphere, the ambient magical energy, the mage-cell inheritance woven into every living thing — all of it provided an alternative power source. The rifles' energy matrices, designed for shipboard power cells, proved compatible with raw magical input. A user with sufficient magical capacity could fire the weapon by channeling their own reserves through the grip.

    The rifle became a magic conduit. Not by design — by accident. By the strange physics of a world where technology and magic share the same substrate.

    Known Surviving Rifles¶

    Fewer than ten pulse rifles are believed to exist on Ge'or. Most are buried, broken, or unrecognized for what they are. Only one is confirmed active:

    Amelia's Rifle¶

    The pulse rifle carried by Amelia of Grimmel Republic is the only confirmed operational unit. It was discovered in 377 AGD by an ancestor of the Amelia family — a hunter who found it half-buried in a cave in the western hills of Grimmel. He discovered its function by accident and named it a lightning bow.

    The rifle has been passed down through eleven generations. Amelia received it from her father on his deathbed in 602 AGD, when she was four years old. It has never malfunctioned. It has never missed.

    Physical description: The weapon resembles an M416 carbine — a design familiar to anyone who served in the Last Great War's ground forces. Compact frame, forward grip, shoulder stock, integrated sight housing. The metal is dull grey, unscratched despite fifteen thousand years. The grip is worn smooth by two centuries of Amelia-family hands. To a medieval eye, it is a strange metal crossbow without a string. To Emrys, it is a ghost.

    Function — Magic as Ammunition¶

    The pulse rifle no longer fires energy bolts from a power cell. It fires concentrated magic drawn from the user's own reserves:

    • The wielder channels magical energy through the grip
    • The rifle's internal matrix compresses and accelerates the magic into a coherent bolt
    • The bolt travels in a straight line at near-instantaneous speed
    • Impact delivers force equivalent to a high-level lightning spell — lethal to unarmored targets, sufficient for small to medium game

    The weapon has no trigger safety, no magazine, no reload mechanism. It fires as long as the wielder has magic to give. A depleted user cannot fire it. A child with strong magical potential — like Amelia, like Emrys — can fire it repeatedly.

    Cultural Context — The Lightning Bow¶

    To the people of Ge'or, the pulse rifle is not a firearm. It is a magical artifact — a lightning bow, a thunder staff, a relic of the dragon age or earlier. No one alive on Ge'or — except Emrys, whose past-life memory recognizes it — knows what it truly is.

    Amelia brags about her "hundreds of confirmed kills" with it. She has hunted wargs, gnolls, and small game. She calls it her lightning bow. She will not be corrected.

    The rifle is the proof that the world Emrys remembers is real. It is the smoking gun of the Last Great War — a piece of Earth, still firing, in the hands of a tsundere in a blue maid dress.
